title: Two Appraisal Formats in One Pipeline: What UAD 3.6 and the Redesigned URAR Change for Automated Appraisal Review
summary: Since November 2, 2026, new appraisal reports submitted to the UCDP must use UAD 3.6, unless the seller holds the GSEs' one-time exception, and UAD 2.6 is not fully retired until June 28, 2027. For the next seven months a pipeline will carry both formats, with different field names, rating rules and findings codes. A technical account of what changed in the data, where automated review breaks if it treats the new report as the old one, and the checks our agents run on each version.
body_markdown:
## Who This Is For


Collateral and appraisal review managers, pre-funding QC leads, and the technology owners who maintain appraisal ingestion at lenders selling to Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac. Also model risk teams whose inventory includes any rule or model that reads appraisal data, because the data under those rules changed this month.


## The Date That Moved, and the One That Did Not


The GSEs' redesign of the Uniform Appraisal Dataset ran in three stages. Limited production opened on September 8, 2025. Broad production began on January 26, 2026, with UAD 2.6 still accepted alongside the new format. Fannie Mae's[Selling Guide announcement SEL-2025-04](https://singlefamily.fanniemae.com/media/42751/display) set the mandate: lenders use UAD 3.6 "for all new appraisal reports submitted to the UCDP on or after Nov. 2, 2026." The trigger is the report's first UCDP submission date, not the application date or the note date.


That date held. What changed, in a joint[temporary policy exception announced on September 30, 2026](https://sf.freddiemac.com/docs/pdf/uad-temporary-policy-exception-sept-2026.pdf) , is the tail. Sellers granted the exception may keep submitting UAD 2.6 reports through February 28, 2027, which the GSEs call "a one-time policy exception that will not be extended." From March 1 to May 19, 2027, 2.6 reports are still accepted but with reduced Collateral Underwriter and Loan Collateral Advisor functionality, and Freddie Mac says a 2.6 report in that window loses appraised-value rep and warranty relief. From May 20 to June 27, 2027, 2.6 is accepted only for resubmitting a report first filed in 2.6. UAD 2.6 is fully retired on June 28, 2027, replacing the May 3, 2027 date in the original[October 2024 joint announcement](https://sf.freddiemac.com/docs/pdf/uad_joint_announcement_oct_2024.pdf) .


The practical result is that a lender's pipeline today holds appraisals in both formats, and will for most of 2027. A loan locked in October with a 2.6 appraisal can close in December next to a loan whose appraisal came in last week as 3.6. A purchase that falls through and is re-appraised for a new contract can produce a 3.6 report on a file that already has a 2.6 one. Any automated review that assumes one format is now wrong on some share of files.


## What the Redesigned URAR Actually Replaces


The redesigned Uniform Residential Appraisal Report is one dynamic form. It covers one-unit properties, condos and manufactured homes, and traditional, hybrid and desktop valuation methods. SEL-2025-04 lists what it retires: forms 1004, 1004C, 1004 Desktop, 1004 Hybrid, 1025, 1073, 1073 Hybrid, 1075, 2055 and 2090. Form 1004D, the appraisal update and completion report, gives way to a standalone Restricted Appraisal Update and Completion Report. The data standard moves from MISMO 2.6 to the MISMO Reference Model 3.6.


For anyone who built extraction around form numbers, that list is the first problem. A rule that said "if the form is a 1073, run the condo project checks" has no form number to key on. The property type and the sections the report contains now carry that information, so the routing logic has to read the data, not the form.


## Five Changes That Break Rules Written for 2.6


We went through our own appraisal checks against the[Fannie Mae UAD 3.6 policy supplement](https://singlefamily.fanniemae.com/media/42571/display) and Freddie Mac's[condition and quality rating definitions](https://sf.freddiemac.com/docs/pdf/uad-condition-quality-ratings-definitions.pdf) , and sorted every check into one of three groups: unchanged, needs a second path for 3.6, or needs rewriting. These are the changes that put checks into the second and third groups.


### Gross living area is gone as a term


UAD 3.6 retires "gross living area" in favour of above-grade finished area and below-grade finished area, measured under ANSI Z765-2021, as[Selling Guide B4-1.3-05](https://selling-guide.fanniemae.com/sel/b4-1.3-05/improvements-section-appraisal-report) describes. Any part of a level that is below grade makes that level below grade. ANSI measurement predates 3.6, and it does not apply to 2-4 unit properties, while apartment-style condo and co-op units use interior measurements.


The trap is comparison across formats. A file with a 2.6 appraisal reporting 2,140 square feet of GLA and a later 3.6 report on the same house showing 1,780 square feet above grade (illustrative numbers) has not necessarily lost 360 square feet. A walk-out lower level that the first appraiser counted and the second classed as below grade explains it. A check that compares the two numbers and flags a 17% drop as a value or fraud signal will raise a false finding, and a check that ignores the change entirely will miss the case where the area really is different.


### Condition and quality ratings kept their labels and changed their meaning


C1 through C6 and Q1 through Q6 survive. The definitions were rewritten. Interior and exterior are now rated separately, with an overall rating for the whole property. C1 carries a 12-month age limit. C2 now means new construction, or a remodel down to the studs, within the last 36 months. Any C6 component makes the whole dwelling C6, and a C6 property must be appraised subject to repairs that bring it to at least C5. When a report is subject to repairs or completion, an "as is" overall condition rating is required as well. The ratings now apply to manufactured homes too.


So a C2 on a 2.6 report and a C2 on a 3.6 report are not the same claim. An eligibility rule written as "condition rating C5 or C6 requires repair conditions" still works, but it now has to read the overall rating, check the as-is rating where the report is subject to repairs, and notice an interior C6 sitting under an exterior C4.


### Defects moved out of the commentary and into the sections


Under 2.6, the description of a defect often lived in the appraiser's free-text comments, and extraction had to find it. Under 3.6, defects, damages and deficiencies are reported inside the section they belong to: Site, Dwelling Exterior, Unit Interior, Outbuilding, Vehicle Storage and Amenities, according to[Freddie Mac's photo and image job aid](https://sf.freddiemac.com/docs/pdf/uad-photo-and-image-job-aid.pdf) . That is better data. It also means a 3.6 check should read the structured defect fields first, and a check that still searches the comments will under-report.


### Photos and the sketch are conditional on the data


In 3.6, each photo is required, conditionally required or optional depending on what the report says, and a missing required photo makes the report incomplete. Report a defect and a photo of it becomes required. The Fannie supplement also lists a floor plan or footprint sketch with calculations as a required exhibit. A static checklist of "front, rear, street, kitchen, bathrooms" no longer describes a complete report. The required set has to be derived from the report itself.


### New sections that did not exist before


The redesign adds a Disaster Mitigation section, with standardized features such as a fortified roof or a storm shelter, and an Energy Efficient and Green Features section covering renewable energy components, building certifications and efficiency ratings. Neither changes eligibility on its own. Both are new fields that a lender's own overlays, its insurance review, or a[pre-close QC check of the hazard policy](https://www.seiright.com/blog/pre-close-qc-title-commitment-hazard-insurance-review-ai-fannie-b7-2-b7-3) may want to read, and a solar array listed in the green features section is a prompt to look for a lease or power purchase agreement in the title work.


## The Findings Changed Too


The appraisal is only half of what comes back from the UCDP. The other half is the Submission Summary Report and the GSEs' proprietary findings. For UAD 3.6, Fannie Mae's messaging guide sorts messages into UCDP system findings, UAD 3.6 compliance rules and Fannie Mae proprietary findings, at five severity levels: Fatal, Severe, Warning, Informational and Notification. A Fatal message means the submission is not successful, and Fannie Mae says critical messages stop its own findings, including the CU risk score, from firing at all. Freddie Mac moved its 3.6 Loan Collateral Advisor messages to[five-digit codes](https://sf.freddiemac.com/articles/news/freddie-mac-collateral-feedback-messages-loan-collateral-advisor-and-ucdp-for-uad-3.6) , while 2.6 messages keep their four-digit codes and the 3.6 messages are returned only on 3.6 submissions.


A rule that clears a condition when "CU score present and below 2.5" now has a failure mode it did not have before. On a 3.6 submission with a critical message, no CU score fires at all. The rule should treat a missing score as an open item with a reason, not as a pass and not as a generic error, and it should read the message codes in the format that matches the report.


## How Our Agents Handle Both Formats


The appraisal review in our[Pre-Close QC Agent](https://www.seiright.com/for-lenders/pre-close-qc-agent) starts by determining which dataset the report is in, from the MISMO version in the XML when we have it and from the report's structure when we only have the PDF. That one field decides which set of rules in the[Rulebook](https://www.seiright.com/how-it-works#rulebook) applies. Both versions write into the same[Loan Graph](https://www.seiright.com/platform/loan-graph) record for the property, but the area fields stay separate: a 2.6 GLA figure is never stored as above-grade finished area, because they are measured to different definitions.


On every appraisal, the agent checks:


- That the format is allowed for the submission date. A 2.6 report first submitted to the UCDP on or after November 2, 2026 is a finding unless the seller holds the exception, and after February 28, 2027 it is a finding regardless.
- That the UCDP status is successful and the findings match the format: four-digit LCA codes on a 2.6 submission, five-digit on a 3.6 one, and no Fatal messages.
- For a 3.6 report, that every conditionally required photo the report's own data calls for is present, along with the sketch and its calculations.
- That the condition rating used for eligibility is the right one: the overall rating, the as-is rating where the report is subject to repairs, and any C6 component.
- Where a file holds two appraisals in different formats, that differences in area and condition are explained by the change in definitions before anything is raised as a value concern.


That last check is the one we deliberately do not automate to a pass. When a 2.6 and a 3.6 report on the same property disagree, the agent lays both figures, both definitions and the relevant pages side by side and hands the file to a collateral reviewer. Whether a lower level is really below grade is a question about the house, and the photos and sketch answer it better than a rule does. Each step runs through[Triple Check](https://www.seiright.com/how-it-works#triple-check) , and anything below its confidence threshold goes to a person as a named exception with the field, the page and the rule.


In the[pre-close QC deployment at Better Mortgage](https://www.seiright.com/case-study/sei-x-nasdaq-lender) , the appraisal is one of more than twenty document types the agent reads across Conventional, FHA, VA and HELOC files, and human review per loan file fell from 4 hours 50 minutes to 47 minutes. During a format transition, that time saving only holds if the checks know which format they are reading.


## What to Do Before June 2027


If you maintain appraisal rules, inventory every one of them that reads a form number, the GLA field, a condition rating or a findings code, and decide for each whether it needs a second path or a rewrite. Under[SR 11-7](https://www.federalreserve.gov/supervisionreg/srletters/sr1107.htm) , a change in the input data to a model is a reason to revalidate it, and that applies to an AVM-reconciliation rule or a CU-score threshold as much as to a statistical model. Ask your appraisal management company which clients it is still delivering 2.6 for and until when, because the exception belongs to the seller, not the AMC. And keep both paths until the last loan with a 2.6 report has been sold, which, as the GSEs point out, can be after June 28, 2027: the retirement "does not preclude the sale of the loan."
